questions.problem: Given the polynomial $P(x)=-{x}^{2}(x+1)(x-2)(x+2),$ find the solution of $P(x)\le 0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)\le 0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies below the $x$-axis or touches this axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)=-{x}^{2}(x+1)(x-2)(x+2)$ are $x=\pm 2,x=-1$ and $x=0,$ where

- $x=\pm 2$ and $x=-1$ are simple roots, and

- $x=0$ has multiplicity $2.$

Also, $P(x)$ is a quintic polynomial with a negative leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033945/assets/1fb947e6360139669bae0821e0de8460da53ead628f589998fab1ce442646cdf.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)\le 0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is below the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in [-2,-1]\cup {0}\cup [2,\infty ).$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Polynomial Inequality Containing No Constant Term
questions.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)>0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis.

First, we factorize the polynomial $P(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & ={x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}-x-2) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+x-2x-2) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x(x+1)-2(x+1)) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x+1)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)={x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}$ are $x=-1,$ $x=0$ and $x=2,$ where

- $x=0$ has multiplicity $2,$ and

- $x=-1$ and $x=2$ are simple roots.

So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033945/assets/c0756761d00b0805683e447d8cee3b657bbbe004a0a47da428927585037b06c2.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)>0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-1)\cup (2,\infty ).$

questions.problem: Given the polynomial $P(x)={x}^{3}(x-1)(x+2)(x-2),$ find the solution of $P(x)<0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)<0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies below the $x$-axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)={x}^{3}(x-1)(x+2)(x-2)$ are $x=0,$ $x=1$ and $x=\pm 2,$ where

- $x=0$ has multiplicity $3,$ and

- $x=1$ and $x=\pm 2$ are simple roots.

Also, $P(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $6$ with a positive leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033945/assets/a37f1c62868581f74a60c073adabf59e2fc66cb17135ffa48df1c76eb22803c8.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)<0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is below the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-2,0)\cup (1,2).$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Polynomial Inequality Containing No Constant Term
questions.worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)>0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis.

First, we factor the polynomial $P(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & ={x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+2x-8) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x+4x-8) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x(x-2)+4(x-2)) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x+4)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)={x}^{4}+3{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}$ are $x=-4,$ $x=0$ and $x=2,$  where

- $x=0$ has multiplicity $2,$ and

- $x=-4$ and $x=2$ are simple roots.

So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033945/assets/a357caad0365f296f87367ee4ac1000f1ea772d0d27650c8340d475ca742828b.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)>0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-4)\cup (2,\infty ).$
